correctness.rationale:
Enomoto's Theorem 5.4 applies for every \(q\ge3\) and positive \(a,b\), and Proposition 5.6 supplies \(K(q,a,b)\ge(q-1)^d d!/H(
u)^2\) for every partition \(
u\) in the required rectangle. With \(q=7\), \(a=2n\), \(b=n\), and \(
u=(n^{2n})\), the dimension vector and length are \((8n,3n)\) and \(11n\). The hook-product formula is exact. Stirling's formula with a summed \(O(n\log n)\) error gives the displayed coefficient \(4+8\log2-7\log3\). Dividing by \(121n^2\) along \(m=11n\) proves the limsup lower bound. The verifier independently checks finite hook products and arithmetic; those checks are not substituted for the asymptotic proof.

originality.rationale: The closest source provides the general inequality but its asymptotic specialization uses \(q=3\) and a square staircase, with endpoint \((1-\log2)/25\). Full-text inspection found no \(q=7\), \(a=2n\), or full-rectangle asymptotic specialization. Scientific searches for the exact constant, seven-arrow specialization, unequal rectangle, and hook-product formulation did not surface an equivalent statement. The main residual risk is the very recent date of the source and incomplete indexing.
residual_risks: The motivating preprint is very recent, so indexing is incomplete and an equivalent unindexed note could exist.
Because the source inequality is general, another reader may independently derive the same specialization even if it has not been stated publicly.
No claim is made that the q=7 full rectangle is globally optimal among all source parameters.

value.rationale: The source explicitly leaves the exact normalized limsup open. The new explicit family raises the published lower endpoint from \((1-\log2)/25\approx0.0122741\) to \((4+8\log2-7\log3)/121\approx0.0153297\), an improvement of about \(24.9\%\). This is a quantitatively meaningful advance on the natural asymptotic invariant, not a finite-table recomputation or arbitrary slice.
